decisions.reason: Although the launch looked narrower and more tentative, it is a specialized hardware product close to the firm's dosimetry core, so sunk development effort and the ability to blame slow uptake on rollout or market timing make management likely to continue it for now.

This chamber was publicly launched and still given its own page in 2019, and because it sits directly in the firm's core measurement portfolio, management is likely to stay committed rather than write off the investment.
As another core ionization-chamber product with visible market presentation across two years, it benefits from strong fit with existing capabilities and escalation-of-commitment pressures to persist.

A standard clinical ionization chamber is central to the firm's established QA business, so prior investment, reputational commitment, and broad clinical relevance make withdrawal unlikely in the next year.

Because this relative-dosimetry chamber complements the firm's main radiation-measurement offering and was publicly maintained after launch, management would be inclined to keep supporting it despite any modest disappointment.
